source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Check onboard nic information
1. Boot into OS.
2. Use tool to check onboard nic information.

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Make sure the information is readable and correct.

deepseek_columns.ai_commands: -- Information check: read the board EEPROM/FRU info ipmitool -I lanplus -C 17 -U "$BMC_USER" -P "$BMC_PASS" -H "$BMC_IP" fru print 2>&1 | head -n 40 ; i2cget -y 2 0x50 0x00 2>&1.
deepseek_columns.ai_logs_output: return the FRU fields + a raw EEPROM read so the user confirms the EEPROM holds valid FRU/product data.

historical_reviews.deepseek: YES; substitutes generic BMC FRU plus guessed host i2c-2/0x50 for onboard NIC information and truncates FRU evidence, creating an unsafe identity mismatch.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: BLOCKED / CHANGED because controller/address/schema and expected values were absent; its I2C safety finding is retained but V3.1 treats resolvable project mapping as readiness.
historical_reviews.round_02: YES; repeats the same unverified I2C target without source-specific NIC mapping.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms no raw transaction may run until the platform owner supplies the exact mapping and semantics.

original_test_intent: Read the approved onboard NIC's EEPROM/identity information through a documented read-only interface and verify the required fields are readable and match the project NIC/board specification.
original_method: Identify the exact onboard NIC and its authoritative EEPROM/firmware information interface, capture the complete read-only field set using the vendor/platform-approved tool and compare each named field with the supplied expected manifest; do not probe guessed I2C targets.
manual_activity: The platform owner supplies the exact NIC target, schema, expected values and safe read method and later issues the verdict. Once mapped, complete information collection and comparison are electronic and can be automated without physical setup.
required_inputs: Exact onboard NIC PCI BDF, vendor/device/subsystem IDs, serial or board location
Definition of the required information fields and authoritative source: NIC EEPROM, NIC firmware inventory or platform FRU
Expected field values and formatting rules
If raw management-bus access is required, exact BMC controller, logical bus, target address, mux path, offset/width and vendor transaction semantics
Approved read-only utility/version, credentials/privilege and recovery boundary
safety_requirements: Do not run i2cget -y 2 0x50 or any guessed raw bus/address transaction.
Do not equate generic BMC FRU data with NIC EEPROM fields unless the platform specification explicitly maps them.
Use read-only commands only, preserve full output and existing logs and protect BMC credentials.
Stop on target ambiguity, mux/controller mismatch, access side effects, inconsistent identities or unexplained data; never probe or retry automatically.
agent_execution_scope: Correlate the supplied physical NIC to PCI, firmware and approved EEPROM/FRU identity and validate the field schema/tool.
Run only the documented read-only inventory or mapped EEPROM transaction and capture complete raw plus decoded output.
Compare each required field to the manifest, collect host/BMC/SEL health and report Tool Result separately from engineer verdict.
engineer_actions: Provide the NIC/EEPROM/controller mapping, field schema and expected values.
Approve the read-only method and any management-bus access boundary.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: ipmitool fru print may be relevant only if the platform maps NIC fields there; head truncation can omit data. The raw i2cget target is unverified and unsafe and one byte cannot prove complete readable/correct NIC information.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Prefer a documented NIC firmware/inventory or platform FRU interface. Use raw BMC-managed I2C only with explicit controller/mux/address/offset/transaction documentation and complete bounded reads.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: Onboard NIC information, readable/correct criterion and 10/0-minute fields are preserved; no target or expected value is invented.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Create a signed NIC information manifest containing physical location, PCI identity, firmware/serial/MAC/FRU fields, authoritative interface and expected values; collect structured read-only data through the safest supported interface.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Exact onboard NIC and board/BMC topology in the manifest.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record NIC firmware/driver, BMC firmware, query tool and OS/kernel versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Use board/NIC vendor EEPROM or inventory documentation and platform BMC bus topology supplied for the target.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces generic/guessed FRU/I2C access with a mapped, field-complete NIC information comparison.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; every owner-required field is compared explicitly rather than one byte or a truncated listing.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: NIC target, schema, expected values and safe interface.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some NIC identity fields may exist in PCI VPD, firmware inventory, a board FRU or a protected EEPROM; those sources are not interchangeable.

project_override_considerations: A project defines the NIC target and field manifest. Missing mappings/specifications delay readiness but do not make the library case permanently BLOCKED or reduce full automation capability.
expected_evidence: SUT/board, physical NIC, PCI/firmware/serial identity and authoritative data-source mapping
Approved tool/version or exact controller/mux/address/transaction definition
Complete raw and decoded read-only information output
Field-by-field expected/actual comparison, no-write/BMC/SEL health, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source consistently asks for onboard NIC information to be readable and correct. The FRU/I2C mismatch appears only in the prior generated command, not in the original procedure or criterion.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The target class and acceptance goal are understandable. Exact NIC/bus/schema details are project readiness inputs; the unsafe guessed command is rejected, but a supplied documented mapping makes the read/comparison fully executable.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects its guessed I2C transaction and generic/truncated FRU evidence while preserving the possibility of electronic readout.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its platform-management/I2C safety gates but reclassifies permanent BLOCKED to FULLY AUTOMATABLE under the V3.1 readiness rule.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Separates target mapping and safe access readiness from automation capability and defines complete field-level evidence.

review_improvement: Prevents writes or side effects on an unknown management bus, avoids confusing board FRU with NIC EEPROM and still provides a precise path to automated verification.
independent_technical_reasoning: The original intent is a read-only onboard-NIC information check. All technical work is automatable once the owner supplies the exact target and schema; missing platform mapping is readiness, not an irreducible semantic blocker, so FULLY AUTOMATABLE is correct.

no_automatic_retry: Do not retry or scan alternate buses/addresses after any access anomaly. Preserve the result and require owner mapping/diagnosis before another read.
